title: Plimpton 322 (Pythagorean triples tablet)
author: Unknown Babylonian scribe
significance: Oldest known list of Pythagorean triples — shows sophisticated number theory 1000+ years before Pythagoras
modernRelevance: The Pythagorean triples on this 3,800-year-old clay tablet use the same number-theoretic relationships that underpin RSA cryptography protecting every online transaction today.

title: MUL.APIN (star catalogue tablets)
author: Babylonian astronomers
significance: Earliest comprehensive star catalogue and astronomical compendium
modernRelevance: The MUL.APIN tablets are the oldest attempt to systematically map the sky, and the tradition of star cataloguing they began runs unbroken through Hipparchus and Ptolemy to the Gaia spacecraft now charting two billion stars.

title: Rhind Mathematical Papyrus
author: Ahmes (scribe)
significance: Major source of ancient Egyptian mathematics — 84 problems covering fractions, geometry, algebra
modernRelevance: The fraction-based algorithms Ahmes recorded are direct ancestors of the fixed-point arithmetic still used in embedded processors and GPU shaders.

title: Moscow Mathematical Papyrus
author: Unknown Egyptian scribe
significance: Contains formula for volume of a frustum — earliest known use of integration-like reasoning

title: Edwin Smith Papyrus
author: Unknown Egyptian physician
significance: Oldest known surgical treatise — rational, empirical approach to 48 trauma cases

title: Ebers Papyrus
author: Unknown Egyptian physician
significance: Most extensive surviving ancient Egyptian medical text — 700+ remedies

title: Sushruta Samhita
author: Sushruta
significance: Ancient Indian surgical text — describes over 300 surgical procedures including rhinoplasty
modernRelevance: Sushruta's rhinoplasty technique, refined over 2,600 years, is the direct ancestor of modern reconstructive surgery, and his emphasis on surgical instruments presaged the precision tooling now used in robotic-assisted operations.

title: Geometric theorems (attributed works)
author: Thales of Miletus
significance: First known use of deductive reasoning in mathematics — the birth of proof
modernRelevance: Thales's insistence that geometric claims require logical proof -- not just measurement -- created the culture of rigorous demonstration that underpins every mathematical proof, software verification, and formal methods system today.

title: On harmonics and number theory (attributed works)
author: Pythagoras and the Pythagorean school
significance: Discovery of mathematical ratios in musical harmony — mathematics as the language of nature
modernRelevance: Pythagoras's discovery that simple integer ratios govern musical consonance was the first evidence that nature obeys mathematical laws -- the founding assumption behind every physics equation from F=ma to the Standard Model.

title: Hippocratic Corpus
author: Hippocrates of Cos and followers
significance: Foundation of Western medicine — disease has natural causes, not divine punishment
modernRelevance: Hippocrates's radical claim that disease has natural, not supernatural, causes is the founding assumption of modern evidence-based medicine -- every clinical trial and epidemiological study rests on this 2,400-year-old insight.

title: On the nature of atoms (reconstructed fragments)
author: Democritus
significance: First atomic theory — all matter is composed of indivisible particles (atomos) moving in void
source: Fragments preserved in Aristotle, Theophrastus, Simplicius
modernRelevance: Every scanning tunneling microscope image of individual atoms vindicates Democritus's 2,400-year-old conjecture that matter is made of indivisible particles in void.

title: Timaeus
author: Plato
significance: First systematic cosmology in Western tradition — geometric model of matter, the world-soul

title: Physics (Φυσικὴ ἀκρόασις)
author: Aristotle
significance: First systematic treatment of motion, causation, and change — dominated physics for 2000 years
modernRelevance: Although Newton replaced Aristotle's mechanics, Aristotle's framework of asking 'why does this move?' established physics as a discipline, and his four causes remain a useful conceptual tool in systems engineering and causal inference.

title: On the Heavens (De Caelo)
author: Aristotle
significance: Geocentric cosmology with crystalline spheres — the standard model until Copernicus

title: History of Animals (Historia Animalium)
author: Aristotle
significance: First systematic biological survey — classified 500+ species, pioneered comparative anatomy

title: Meteorologica
author: Aristotle
significance: First systematic treatment of weather, climate, and geological processes

title: Elements (Στοιχεῖα)
author: Euclid of Alexandria
significance: The most influential mathematics textbook ever written — axiomatic method, 465 propositions in 13 books. Standard for 2000+ years
source: Multiple traditions; Heath translation; Heiberg critical edition
modernRelevance: The axiomatic method Euclid invented is still how every mathematics paper, formal software verification proof, and automated theorem prover is structured today.

title: Optics
author: Euclid of Alexandria
significance: First geometric treatment of vision and perspective

title: On the Sizes and Distances of the Sun and Moon
author: Aristarchus of Samos
significance: First known attempt to determine astronomical distances using geometry; also proposed heliocentrism
modernRelevance: The geometric parallax technique Aristarchus pioneered is the same method the Gaia spacecraft uses today to measure distances to two billion stars in our galaxy.

title: The Method of Mechanical Theorems
author: Archimedes
significance: Archimedes reveals how he discovered theorems using infinitesimal methods — anticipates integral calculus by 1900 years
modernRelevance: Archimedes's infinitesimal slicing technique is the conceptual ancestor of every numerical integration algorithm running in engineering simulations worldwide.

title: The Sand Reckoner (Ψαμμίτης)
author: Archimedes
significance: First system for expressing astronomically large numbers; estimates grains of sand to fill the universe

title: On Floating Bodies
author: Archimedes
significance: Foundation of hydrostatics — Archimedes' principle of buoyancy
modernRelevance: Archimedes' principle of buoyancy is applied every day in naval architecture, submarine ballast systems, and the hydrometer sensors that monitor battery acid density in your car.

title: On the Sphere and Cylinder
author: Archimedes
significance: Derives surface area and volume of spheres — his proudest result, engraved on his tombstone

title: On the Equilibrium of Planes
author: Archimedes
significance: Foundation of statics and the theory of the lever — first rigorous treatment of centers of gravity

title: On the Measurement of the Earth
author: Eratosthenes of Cyrene
significance: First accurate measurement of Earth's circumference using shadow angles — correct to within 2%
modernRelevance: Eratosthenes's shadow-angle method is the conceptual basis of satellite geodesy, and his 2% accurate result stood as the best measurement of Earth's size for over a thousand years.

title: Conics (Κωνικά)
author: Apollonius of Perga
significance: Definitive treatment of conic sections (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) — essential for Kepler's orbits 1800 years later
source: Books I-IV in Greek (Heiberg); V-VII in Arabic translation
modernRelevance: Every planetary orbit, cometary trajectory, and gravity-assist flyby calculated at NASA is a conic section -- the same ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas Apollonius classified 2,200 years ago.

title: Star catalogue and precession discovery
author: Hipparchus of Nicaea
significance: First comprehensive star catalogue (850+ stars with positions); discovered precession of equinoxes
source: Known through Ptolemy's Almagest; original lost
modernRelevance: Hipparchus's magnitude system for star brightness, invented 2,100 years ago, is still the basis of the apparent magnitude scale astronomers use at every observatory on Earth.

title: De Rerum Natura (On the Nature of Things)
author: Lucretius
significance: Epic poem presenting Epicurean atomic physics — matter is atoms in void, no divine intervention in nature

title: Pneumatics
author: Hero of Alexandria
significance: Describes the aeolipile (first known steam engine), siphons, force pumps, and automata

title: Metrica
author: Hero of Alexandria
significance: Contains Heron's formula for triangle area; practical algorithms for volumes and areas

title: Naturalis Historia
author: Pliny the Elder
significance: 37-volume encyclopedia — the most comprehensive surviving work on natural knowledge from antiquity

title: Almagest (Μαθηματικὴ Σύνταξις)
author: Claudius Ptolemy
significance: Definitive geocentric astronomical model — mathematical machinery for predicting planetary positions. Standard for 1400 years
modernRelevance: Ptolemy's epicycle machinery was so accurate it was used to predict eclipses and planetary positions for 1,400 years, and his coordinate system is the direct ancestor of modern celestial coordinates.

title: Geography (Γεωγραφικὴ Ὑφήγησις)
author: Claudius Ptolemy
significance: Coordinate system for mapping the known world — latitude, longitude, and map projections
modernRelevance: Ptolemy's latitude-longitude grid and map projection techniques are the direct ancestors of the coordinate systems used by GPS, Google Maps, and every GIS platform on the planet.

title: On Anatomical Procedures
author: Galen of Pergamon
significance: Most influential anatomical work until Vesalius — dominated medical education for 1300 years

title: Arithmetica
author: Diophantus of Alexandria
significance: First systematic treatment of algebraic equations — Fermat's marginal note in this book launched modern number theory
modernRelevance: Diophantine equations -- integer solutions to polynomial equations -- are now central to modern cryptography, coding theory, and the elliptic-curve methods that proved Fermat's Last Theorem 1,700 years after Diophantus wrote.

title: Mathematical Collection (Synagoge)
author: Pappus of Alexandria
significance: Summarizes and extends classical Greek geometry — includes the Pappus theorem and centroid theorem

title: Aryabhatiya
author: Aryabhata
significance: Indian mathematical masterwork — sine tables, place-value system, Earth's rotation, planetary periods
source: Multiple Sanskrit manuscripts; Shukla & Sarma edition
modernRelevance: Aryabhata's sine tables and place-value system traveled west through Arab mathematicians and became the computational infrastructure of modern science -- every digital calculator descends from his notation.

title: Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta
author: Brahmagupta
significance: First systematic treatment of zero as a number, negative numbers, and quadratic equations with two roots
modernRelevance: Brahmagupta's rules for zero and negative numbers are executed billions of times per second in every computer's arithmetic logic unit -- without his formalization, modern computing would have no foundation.

title: De Temporum Ratione (The Reckoning of Time)
author: The Venerable Bede
significance: Established the AD dating system and computed Easter tables — foundation of medieval timekeeping

title: Corpus Jabirianum (collected chemical works)
author: Jābir ibn Hayyān
significance: Pioneered systematic experimental chemistry — distillation, crystallization, acid synthesis
modernRelevance: Jabir's distillation and crystallization techniques, refined over 1,200 years, are still the core purification methods used in pharmaceutical manufacturing and chemical engineering worldwide.

title: Al-Kitāb al-Mukhtaṣar fī Ḥisāb al-Jabr wal-Muqābala
author: Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī
significance: The book that gave algebra its name — systematic methods for solving linear and quadratic equations
modernRelevance: The word 'algorithm' derives from al-Khwarizmi's name, and his systematic equation-solving methods are the direct ancestor of every computer program ever written.

title: On the Calculation with Hindu Numerals
author: Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī
significance: Introduced Hindu-Arabic numerals and positional notation to the Islamic world and later Europe. 'Algorithm' derives from his name

title: De Aspectibus (On Optics)
author: Al-Kindī
significance: Advanced the science of optics — argued light travels in straight lines, analyzed reflection

title: Kitab al-Hawi fi al-tibb (Liber Continens)
author: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī (Rhazes)
significance: Largest medieval medical encyclopedia — distinguished smallpox from measles, pioneered clinical observation

title: Kitāb az-Zīj (Astronomical Tables)
author: Al-Battānī
significance: Most accurate pre-telescopic star positions and planetary parameters — refined Ptolemy's values significantly

title: Iḥṣāʾ al-ʿUlūm (Enumeration of the Sciences)
author: Al-Fārābī
significance: First systematic classification of all sciences — influenced medieval European university curricula

title: Al-Qānūn fī al-Ṭibb (The Canon of Medicine)
author: Ibn Sīnā (Avicenna)
significance: The standard medical textbook in Europe and the Islamic world for 600 years — systematic, encyclopedic, rational
modernRelevance: Ibn Sina's insistence on clinical trials, his classification of over 700 drugs, and his systematic diagnostic framework prefigure the evidence-based pharmacology that governs modern FDA drug approvals.

title: Kitāb al-Manāẓir (Book of Optics)
author: Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen)
significance: Foundation of modern optics — refuted emission theory of vision, described the camera obscura, pioneered experimental scientific method
modernRelevance: Alhazen's camera obscura principle and his insistence on experimental verification of optical theories directly prefigure every modern camera sensor and the scientific method itself.

title: Tārīkh al-Hind (History of India)
author: Abū Rayḥān al-Bīrūnī
significance: Calculated Earth's radius to within 16 km of modern value; pioneered comparative scientific study across cultures

title: Risāla fī al-barāhīn ʿalā masāʾil al-jabr wa al-muqābala (Treatise on algebra)
author: Omar Khayyām
significance: First systematic treatment of cubic equations using conic section intersections — geometric algebra at its peak

title: Mengxi Bitan (Dream Pool Essays)
author: Shen Kuo
significance: Describes the magnetic compass for navigation, movable type printing, fossils as evidence of climate change, and geological uplift

title: Al-Tadhkira fī ʿilm al-hayʾa (Memoir on Astronomy)
author: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī
significance: The Tusi couple — a mathematical device that converts circular motion into linear. Likely influenced Copernicus

title: Opus Majus
author: Roger Bacon
significance: Advocated for experimental science and mathematics as foundations of knowledge — described optics, lenses, and gunpowder

title: Liber Abaci
author: Leonardo Fibonacci
significance: Introduced Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe and presented the Fibonacci sequence. Changed European commerce and mathematics
modernRelevance: The Hindu-Arabic numeral system Fibonacci brought to Europe is the universal notation of global commerce, and Fibonacci numbers appear in everything from phyllotaxis to financial trading algorithms.

title: De Luce (On Light)
author: Robert Grosseteste
significance: Proposed that light is the fundamental substance of the universe — proto-physics of radiation, influenced Roger Bacon

title: De configurationibus qualitatum et motuum
author: Nicole Oresme
significance: Graphed velocity against time — first use of coordinate geometry, anticipated Descartes by 300 years; proved the mean speed theorem

title: Kerala school infinite series expansions
author: Mādhava of Saṅgamagrāma
significance: Discovered infinite series for π, sine, cosine, and arctangent — 250 years before Newton and Leibniz
source: Yuktibhāṣā (1530, by Jyeṣṭhadeva, recording Mādhava's work)
modernRelevance: Madhava's infinite series for pi and trigonometric functions, discovered 250 years before Newton, are the same Taylor series expansions computed trillions of times per second in scientific software.

title: Al-Muqaddimah (The Introduction)
author: Ibn Khaldūn
significance: Foundation of sociology, demography, and philosophy of history — cyclical theory of civilizations

title: Zīj-i Sulṭānī (star catalogue)
author: Ulugh Beg
significance: Most accurate star catalogue before Tycho Brahe — positions of 1018 stars from the Samarkand Observatory

title: Gutenberg Bible (first major printed book)
author: Johannes Gutenberg
significance: Movable type printing press — enabled the Scientific Revolution by making knowledge reproducible and distributable
source: Multiple surviving copies; LOC, British Library, etc.
modernRelevance: Gutenberg's press was the first information technology to achieve mass scale, and its core principle -- cheap, exact replication of knowledge -- is the same principle that drives the internet, open-access journals, and arXiv today.

title: De Triangulis Omnimodis
author: Regiomontanus (Johann Müller)
significance: First comprehensive European trigonometry textbook — systematized the field as independent from astronomy

title: De Revolutionibus Orbium Coelestium
author: Nicolaus Copernicus
significance: The heliocentric model — Earth orbits the Sun. Launched the Copernican Revolution and modern astronomy
modernRelevance: The heliocentric shift Copernicus launched is so fundamental that 'Copernican revolution' is still the metaphor scientists use when an entire field's assumptions get overturned.

title: De Humani Corporis Fabrica
author: Andreas Vesalius
significance: First accurate human anatomy based on dissection rather than Galen's authority — stunning illustrations, empirical method
modernRelevance: Vesalius's principle that anatomy must be learned by direct observation, not authority, is the same empirical standard modern medical schools follow, and his detailed illustrations pioneered the anatomical atlases now rendered in 3D for surgical planning.

title: Ars Magna
author: Gerolamo Cardano
significance: Published solutions to cubic and quartic equations — first appearance of complex numbers (even though Cardano distrusted them)
modernRelevance: The complex numbers Cardano reluctantly introduced are now indispensable in electrical engineering, quantum mechanics, and signal processing -- they describe alternating current, quantum states, and Fourier transforms.

title: Astronomiae Instauratae Mechanica
author: Tycho Brahe
significance: Most precise pre-telescopic astronomical observations — the data that enabled Kepler's laws
modernRelevance: Brahe's obsessive precision in measuring planetary positions -- without a telescope -- produced the dataset from which Kepler derived elliptical orbits, proving that good data is the foundation of every scientific revolution.

title: De Magnete
author: William Gilbert
significance: First major experimental physics treatise — Earth is a giant magnet, distinguishes electricity from magnetism
modernRelevance: Gilbert's discovery that Earth is a giant magnet is the foundation of geophysics, and understanding Earth's magnetosphere is critical to NIAC concepts like the CREW HaT radiation shielding system that protects astronauts from cosmic rays.

title: Astronomia Nova
author: Johannes Kepler
significance: Planets orbit in ellipses (first two laws of planetary motion) — replaced 2000 years of circular orbits
modernRelevance: Every orbit calculation at NASA and ESA, from Mars landings to James Webb's halo orbit at L2, begins with Kepler's laws of elliptical planetary motion.

title: Sidereus Nuncius (Starry Messenger)
author: Galileo Galilei
significance: First telescopic observations — moons of Jupiter, craters on the Moon, stars in the Milky Way. Changed what 'observation' means in science
modernRelevance: Galileo's discovery of Jupiter's moons using a homemade telescope directly inspired every space telescope from Hubble to JWST and proved that observation technology can rewrite cosmology overnight.

title: Mirifici Logarithmorum Canonis Descriptio
author: John Napier
significance: Invented logarithms — transformed astronomical calculation, navigation, and engineering for 350 years until computers
modernRelevance: Logarithmic scales remain essential in science and engineering -- the decibel, the Richter scale, pH, and the log-loss functions in machine learning all rely on the computational shortcut Napier invented.

title: Harmonices Mundi
author: Johannes Kepler
significance: Third law of planetary motion (P² ∝ a³) — the bridge between observational data and Newton's gravity

title: Novum Organum
author: Francis Bacon
significance: Laid out the inductive method — the intellectual framework for modern experimental science
modernRelevance: Bacon's inductive method -- observe, hypothesize, experiment, refine -- is the backbone of every scientific grant proposal, peer-reviewed experiment, and Technology Readiness Level assessment NASA uses to evaluate NIAC concepts.

title: De Motu Cordis (On the Motion of the Heart and Blood)
author: William Harvey
significance: Discovered the circulation of blood — overturned Galen's 1400-year-old model with experimental evidence
modernRelevance: Harvey's model of blood as a circulating fluid powered by a pump is the foundation of cardiology, and his approach -- measuring flow rates and volumes to test a theory -- is the template for every physiological experiment in space medicine aboard the ISS.

title: Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems
author: Galileo Galilei
significance: Made the case for heliocentrism in vernacular Italian — got Galileo tried by the Inquisition

title: La Géométrie
author: René Descartes
significance: Invented analytic (coordinate) geometry — merged algebra and geometry, enabling calculus
source: Leiden 1637 (appendix to Discours de la Méthode); Smith & Latham translation
modernRelevance: The x-y coordinate plane Descartes invented is the foundation of every graph, screen pixel grid, GPS coordinate, and data visualization on the planet.

title: Discours de la Méthode
author: René Descartes
significance: 'Cogito ergo sum' — established rationalism and systematic doubt as methods of inquiry

title: Marginal note in Arithmetica (Fermat's Last Theorem)
author: Pierre de Fermat
significance: 'I have discovered a truly marvelous proof, which this margin is too narrow to contain.' Took 358 years to prove (Wiles, 1995)
source: Fermat's copy of Diophantus; now lost; statement known from Samuel de Fermat's 1670 publication

title: Correspondence with Fermat on probability
author: Blaise Pascal & Pierre de Fermat
significance: Founded probability theory — the 'problem of points' and expected value. Basis for insurance, statistics, and decision theory
modernRelevance: The expected-value framework Pascal and Fermat invented in this correspondence is the mathematical engine behind every Monte Carlo simulation, financial risk model, and probabilistic mission-planning tool at NASA.

title: Pensées (and the hydraulic press, 1653)
author: Blaise Pascal
significance: Pascal's law — pressure is transmitted equally in enclosed fluids. Foundation of hydraulics

title: The Sceptical Chymist
author: Robert Boyle
significance: Rejected Aristotelian four-element theory — defined elements as substances that cannot be broken down further
modernRelevance: Boyle's operational definition of an element -- a substance that cannot be broken into simpler substances -- is still the working definition used in chemistry, and his skeptical method of demanding experimental proof over tradition became the gold standard of science.

title: Micrographia
author: Robert Hooke
significance: First great work of microscopy — coined the word 'cell' upon seeing cork structure. Stunning illustrations
modernRelevance: Hooke's coinage of the word 'cell' launched cell biology, and the microscopy tradition he pioneered now reaches atomic resolution with cryo-EM, the technique that enabled AlphaFold's training data.

title: Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica
author: Isaac Newton
significance: The most important scientific book ever written. Laws of motion, universal gravitation, calculus applied to physics. Unified terrestrial and celestial mechanics
modernRelevance: SpaceX's Falcon 9 booster lands itself using the same F=ma and gravitational equations Newton published in 1687 -- classical mechanics still guides nearly all space missions.

title: Traité de la Lumière
author: Christiaan Huygens
significance: Wave theory of light — Huygens' principle explains reflection, refraction, and double refraction
modernRelevance: Huygens's wave principle is directly applied in phased-array radar, 5G beamforming antennas, and every ultrasound machine imaging a fetus in a hospital today.

title: Nova Methodus pro Maximis et Minimis (New Method for Maxima and Minima)
author: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
significance: Published differential calculus — the notation (dx, dy, ∫) we still use today. Independent of Newton
modernRelevance: The dx/dy notation Leibniz introduced in 1684 is the exact notation still taught in every calculus class worldwide and used in every differential equation solver.

title: De Geometria Recondita (integral calculus)
author: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
significance: Published integral calculus and the fundamental theorem — completed the framework

title: Opticks
author: Isaac Newton
significance: Particle theory of light, prism experiments revealing the spectrum, theory of color — includes the 'Queries' speculating on deep physics
modernRelevance: Newton's discovery that white light is a mixture of colors is the principle behind every spectrograph used in astronomy today, including the instruments on JWST that identify chemical compositions of exoplanet atmospheres.

title: Hydrodynamica
author: Daniel Bernoulli
significance: Bernoulli's principle — faster fluid = lower pressure. Foundation of aerodynamics and flight
modernRelevance: Bernoulli's principle governs the lift on every aircraft wing and is used in the aerodynamic modeling of NIAC atmospheric entry concepts, from Venus landers to Mars airships like the Evacuated Airship concept.

title: Introductio in Analysin Infinitorum
author: Leonhard Euler
significance: Unified algebra, trigonometry, and calculus — introduced e, standardized notation, defined functions as the central concept

title: Mechanica
author: Leonhard Euler
significance: Reformulated Newtonian mechanics using analysis — made calculus the language of physics

title: Solutio problematis ad geometriam situs pertinentis (Königsberg bridges)
author: Leonhard Euler
significance: Founded graph theory and topology by proving the Seven Bridges of Königsberg has no solution
modernRelevance: The graph theory Euler founded with this playful problem now powers internet routing protocols, social network analysis, Google's PageRank, and the circuit layout algorithms that design every microchip.

title: Various papers on e^(iπ) + 1 = 0
author: Leonhard Euler
significance: Euler's identity — connects the five most important constants in mathematics in one equation. 'The most beautiful theorem in mathematics'
source: Introductio in Analysin Infinitorum and subsequent papers
modernRelevance: Euler's identity e^(i*pi)+1=0 is not just beautiful -- the complex exponential it represents is the workhorse of signal processing in every cellphone, MRI machine, and audio codec.

title: Systema Naturae
author: Carl Linnaeus
significance: Binomial nomenclature system for classifying all living things — still in use today
modernRelevance: Every species discovered in a deep-sea vent, an Amazonian canopy, or a Martian soil sample would be classified using the same two-name system Linnaeus invented -- it remains the universal language of biological taxonomy.

title: Histoire Naturelle (44 volumes)
author: Georges-Louis Leclerc, Comte de Buffon
significance: Most widely read scientific work of the 18th century — estimated Earth's age, proposed continental drift, proto-evolution

title: An Essay towards solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances
author: Thomas Bayes (published posthumously by Richard Price)
significance: Bayes' theorem — foundation of Bayesian inference, now used in machine learning, medicine, and AI
source: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 53 (1763)
modernRelevance: Bayesian inference is the mathematical engine behind spam filters, medical diagnostic AI, autonomous vehicle perception, and the probabilistic reasoning in large language models like Claude and GPT.

title: Mécanique Analytique
author: Joseph-Louis Lagrange
significance: Reformulated all of mechanics using calculus of variations — no diagrams, pure analysis. Lagrangian mechanics
modernRelevance: Lagrangian mechanics is how modern physicists write down the laws of nature, and the Lagrange points L1-L5 that Lagrange discovered are the preferred parking spots for JWST, LISA, and dozens of NIAC mission concepts.

title: Mémoires sur l'Électricité et le Magnétisme
author: Charles-Augustin de Coulomb
significance: Coulomb's law — electric force between charges follows an inverse-square law, like gravity
source: Mémoires de l'Académie Royale des Sciences, 1785-1789

title: Traité Élémentaire de Chimie
author: Antoine Lavoisier
significance: Founded modern chemistry — conservation of mass, oxygen theory of combustion, systematic nomenclature. 'The Chemical Revolution'
modernRelevance: Lavoisier's insistence on precise mass measurement and systematic nomenclature established the framework every pharmaceutical lab and chemical plant on Earth operates under today.

title: Experiments to Determine the Density of the Earth
author: Henry Cavendish
significance: First measurement of the gravitational constant G — 'weighed the Earth' using a torsion balance
source: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 88 (1798)
modernRelevance: The gravitational constant G that Cavendish measured is a required input for every orbit calculation, spacecraft trajectory, and gravity-assist maneuver -- including NIAC concepts like the Solar Gravity Lens mission.

title: An Inquiry into the Causes and Effects of the Variolae Vaccinae
author: Edward Jenner
significance: Demonstrated vaccination against smallpox using cowpox — foundation of immunology, saved hundreds of millions of lives
modernRelevance: Jenner's principle of using a weakened pathogen to train the immune system was applied directly in the mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, and vaccination remains the single medical intervention that has saved the most human lives in history.

title: Disquisitiones Arithmeticae
author: Carl Friedrich Gauss
significance: Foundation of modern number theory — quadratic reciprocity, modular arithmetic, construction of regular polygons
modernRelevance: Gauss's modular arithmetic is the mathematical engine inside every modern encryption system, from AES to elliptic-curve cryptography protecting billions of internet connections.

title: On the Theory of Light and Colours (Bakerian Lecture)
author: Thomas Young
significance: Double-slit experiment proving wave nature of light — one of the most beautiful experiments in physics
source: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 92 (1802)
modernRelevance: Young's double-slit experiment is still performed with single electrons and photons to demonstrate quantum superposition, and wave interference is the operating principle behind LIGO's gravitational wave detectors.

title: A New System of Chemical Philosophy
author: John Dalton
significance: Modern atomic theory — elements are made of atoms, atoms of the same element are identical, compounds form in fixed ratios
modernRelevance: Dalton's atomic theory gave chemistry its quantitative foundation -- the stoichiometric ratios he established are used in every chemical reaction calculation, from ISRU propellant production on Mars to pharmaceutical synthesis.

title: Théorie Analytique de la Chaleur
author: Jean-Baptiste Joseph Fourier
significance: Fourier analysis — any function can be decomposed into sine waves. Foundation of signal processing, quantum mechanics, and data science
modernRelevance: The FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) based on Fourier's decomposition runs in every audio codec, MRI scanner, seismograph, and deep-space communication link -- it may be the most widely executed algorithm on Earth.

title: Réflexions sur la Puissance Motrice du Feu
author: Sadi Carnot
significance: Founded thermodynamics — Carnot cycle, efficiency limits on heat engines, the concept of entropy (implicit)
modernRelevance: Carnot's efficiency limit is the hard ceiling every power-generation system must respect, from terrestrial gas turbines to the NIAC APPLE nuclear reactor concept and every radioisotope thermoelectric generator on deep-space probes.

title: On the Principles of Geometry
author: Nikolai Lobachevsky
significance: Non-Euclidean geometry — parallel postulate is independent. Later essential for general relativity
modernRelevance: Lobachevsky's proof that consistent non-Euclidean geometries exist opened the door for Riemann and ultimately Einstein -- without it, general relativity's curved spacetime would have had no mathematical language.

title: Principles of Geology
author: Charles Lyell
significance: Uniformitarianism — geological processes are slow, gradual, and ongoing. Gave Darwin the deep time he needed for evolution
modernRelevance: Lyell's uniformitarianism -- the idea that present processes explain past geology -- is the operating assumption of planetary science, from interpreting Martian river channels to analyzing the geology of Titan.

title: Experimental Researches in Electricity (series)
author: Michael Faraday
significance: Discovered electromagnetic induction, laws of electrolysis, the Faraday effect — pure experimental genius with no formal mathematics
modernRelevance: Faraday's discovery of electromagnetic induction is literally what generates the electricity you are using right now -- every power plant turbine on Earth exploits this effect.

title: On Quaternions; or on a New System of Imaginaries in Algebra
author: William Rowan Hamilton
significance: Discovered quaternions — first example of a non-commutative algebra, now essential for 3D rotations and computer graphics
source: Proceedings of the Royal Irish Academy, multiple papers 1843-1850

title: On the Mechanical Equivalent of Heat
author: James Prescott Joule
significance: Established that heat is a form of energy — measured the mechanical equivalent of heat, confirming energy conservation
source: Philosophical Magazine and British Association reports, 1845-1850

title: On the Moving Force of Heat (Über die bewegende Kraft der Wärme)
author: Rudolf Clausius
significance: Formulated the second law of thermodynamics and introduced the concept of entropy

title: Über die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen
author: Bernhard Riemann
significance: Riemannian geometry — curved spaces of arbitrary dimension. The mathematical framework Einstein later used for general relativity
modernRelevance: Every GPS satellite computes corrections for general-relativistic time dilation using Riemannian geometry -- curved spacetime math runs in your phone's location chip.

title: Über die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse
author: Bernhard Riemann
significance: Introduced the Riemann zeta function and stated the Riemann Hypothesis — the most important unsolved problem in mathematics (167 years and counting)

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
significance: The theory of evolution by natural selection — the most transformative idea in biology. Changed humanity's self-understanding
source: London, John Murray, 1859; six editions through 1872
modernRelevance: Evolutionary algorithms directly inspired by Darwin's natural selection are used today to optimize everything from aircraft wing shapes to neural network architectures.

title: Mémoire sur les corpuscules organisés qui existent dans l'atmosphère
author: Louis Pasteur
significance: Disproved spontaneous generation, established germ theory of disease — foundation of microbiology, sterilization, vaccination
modernRelevance: Pasteur's germ theory is the reason we sterilize surgical instruments, pasteurize milk, and maintain sterile cleanrooms when assembling planetary probes -- NASA's planetary protection protocols descend directly from his work.

title: A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field
author: James Clerk Maxwell
significance: Maxwell's equations — unified electricity, magnetism, and light. Predicted electromagnetic waves. Einstein called it 'the most profound and the most fruitful that physics has experienced since the time of Newton'
source: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 155 (1865)
modernRelevance: Maxwell's equations govern the design of every antenna, fiber-optic cable, microchip, and wireless device -- the entire $5 trillion telecommunications industry rests on four equations from 1865.

title: On the Relationship of the Properties of the Elements to their Atomic Weights
author: Dmitri Mendeleev
significance: The periodic table — organized elements by atomic weight, predicted undiscovered elements (gallium, germanium, scandium) correctly
source: Journal of the Russian Chemical Society 1 (1869)
modernRelevance: Mendeleev's periodic table predicted elements before they were found, and today it guides the synthesis of new materials from superconductors to cancer-targeting radioisotopes.

title: Versuche über Pflanzenhybriden (Experiments on Plant Hybridization)
author: Gregor Mendel
significance: Discovered the laws of heredity — dominant and recessive traits, 3:1 ratios. Ignored for 34 years, then rediscovered and transformed biology
source: Verhandlungen des naturforschenden Vereines in Brünn 4 (1866)
modernRelevance: Mendel's laws of inheritance are the foundation of modern genetics, and his insight that traits are encoded in discrete units is the conceptual framework behind CRISPR gene editing and the entire $30 billion genomics industry.

title: Weitere Studien über das Wärmegleichgewicht unter Gasmolekülen
author: Ludwig Boltzmann
significance: H-theorem and statistical interpretation of the second law — entropy as probability. S = k log W
modernRelevance: Boltzmann's S=k*log(W) connects microscopic randomness to macroscopic thermodynamics, and his statistical framework underpins machine learning loss functions, Monte Carlo simulations, and modern statistical physics.

title: Über eine Eigenschaft des Inbegriffes aller reellen algebraischen Zahlen
author: Georg Cantor
significance: Founded set theory — proved the reals are uncountable (different sizes of infinity). Diagonal argument (1891) followed
source: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 77 (1874)
modernRelevance: Cantor's proof that infinities come in different sizes is the foundation of modern mathematical logic, and set theory remains the axiomatic bedrock on which all of mathematics is formally built.

title: On the Equilibrium of Heterogeneous Substances
author: J. Willard Gibbs
significance: Unified chemical thermodynamics — phase rule, chemical potential, free energy. 'The Principia of thermodynamics'
modernRelevance: Gibbs free energy is the quantity every chemist and materials scientist calculates to predict whether a reaction will occur spontaneously -- it governs battery design, metallurgy, and the ISRU chemical processing proposed for lunar and Martian habitats.

title: Über electrodynamische Wellen im Luftraume und deren Reflexion
author: Heinrich Hertz
significance: First experimental confirmation of electromagnetic waves — proved Maxwell's theory correct. Enabled radio, radar, and wireless communication
modernRelevance: Hertz's experimental proof that electromagnetic waves exist launched the entire wireless revolution -- from radio to Wi-Fi to the Deep Space Network that communicates with spacecraft billions of miles away.

title: Versuch einer Theorie der electrischen und optischen Erscheinungen in bewegten Körpern
author: Hendrik Lorentz
significance: Lorentz transformations — the mathematical framework Einstein later reinterpreted as special relativity

title: Über eine neue Art von Strahlen (On a New Kind of Rays)
author: Wilhelm Röntgen
significance: Discovered X-rays — first Nobel Prize in Physics (1901). Transformed medicine, crystallography, and atomic physics
source: Sitzungsberichte der Physikalisch-Medizinische Gesellschaft zu Würzburg (1895)
modernRelevance: X-ray imaging is used in everything from medical CT scanners to airport security to the X-ray crystallography that revealed DNA's structure and now maps protein structures for drug design.

title: Sur les radiations émises par phosphorescence
author: Henri Becquerel
significance: Discovered radioactivity — uranium salts emit penetrating rays without external energy input
source: Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences 122 (1896)

title: Cathode Rays
author: J.J. Thomson
significance: Discovered the electron — first subatomic particle. Showed atoms have internal structure
modernRelevance: Thomson's electron is the particle whose controlled flow constitutes every electrical current, every transistor switch, and every signal in every computer on Earth -- the entire electronics industry exists because he found it.

title: Analysis Situs
author: Henri Poincaré
significance: Founded algebraic topology — Betti numbers, fundamental group, Poincaré conjecture (proved by Perelman in 2003, 108 years later)

title: Mathematische Probleme (23 problems)
author: David Hilbert
significance: 23 unsolved problems that shaped 20th-century mathematics — some still open. Defined the research agenda of a century
modernRelevance: Several of Hilbert's 23 problems remain unsolved -- the Riemann Hypothesis (Problem 8) carries a $1 million Clay prize, and the questions Hilbert posed about the foundations of mathematics led directly to Godel's incompleteness theorems and Turing's theory of computation.

title: Über das Gesetz der Energieverteilung im Normalspektrum
author: Max Planck
significance: Birth of quantum theory — energy is emitted in discrete quanta (E = hν), not continuously. Solved the black-body radiation problem
modernRelevance: The quantization of energy Planck introduced is the reason semiconductors work, making possible every transistor in the estimated 1 trillion chips manufactured annually.

title: Über einen die Erzeugung und Verwandlung des Lichtes betreffenden heuristischen Gesichtspunkt
author: Albert Einstein
significance: Light comes in quanta (photons) — explained the photoelectric effect. Nobel Prize 1921. One of four groundbreaking 1905 papers
modernRelevance: The photoelectric effect Einstein explained is the operating principle of every solar panel on Earth and in space -- including the solar arrays on the ISS and the photovoltaic cells powering NIAC solar sail missions.

title: Über die von der molekularkinetischen Theorie der Wärme geforderte Bewegung
author: Albert Einstein
significance: Explained Brownian motion — proved atoms exist as real physical entities, not just theoretical conveniences

title: Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper
author: Albert Einstein
significance: Special relativity — speed of light is constant for all observers, time and space are relative. Overturned Newtonian absolute space and time
modernRelevance: Particle accelerators at CERN and Fermilab rely on special relativity for every beam calculation, and E=mc^2 explains why the Sun shines and nuclear reactors produce energy.

title: Ist die Trägheit eines Körpers von seinem Energieinhalt abhängig?
author: Albert Einstein
significance: E = mc² — mass and energy are equivalent. The most famous equation in physics. Foundation of nuclear energy
modernRelevance: E=mc^2 is the equation behind every nuclear reactor, every PET scan in medicine, and every NIAC fusion propulsion concept -- the Pulsed Fission-Fusion engine and Lattice Confinement Fusion both convert mass to energy per Einstein's formula.

title: Die Grundgleichungen für die elektromagnetischen Vorgänge in bewegten Körpern
author: Hermann Minkowski
significance: Reformulated special relativity as geometry of 4D spacetime — 'Henceforth space by itself, and time by itself, are doomed to fade away'

title: The Scattering of α and β Particles by Matter and the Structure of the Atom
author: Ernest Rutherford
significance: Discovered the atomic nucleus — most of the atom is empty space with a tiny, dense, positively charged core
modernRelevance: Rutherford's nuclear model revealed that atomic energy is concentrated in a tiny core, opening the path to nuclear fission and fusion -- the energy sources behind both terrestrial reactors and NIAC nuclear propulsion concepts.

title: On the Constitution of Atoms and Molecules
author: Niels Bohr
significance: Bohr model of the atom — electrons orbit in quantized energy levels, explaining spectral lines

title: Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie
author: Albert Einstein
significance: General relativity — gravity is the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. Predicts black holes, gravitational waves, expansion of the universe
modernRelevance: Every GPS satellite computes corrections for general-relativistic time dilation -- without Einstein's 1915 theory, your phone's location would drift by 10 km per day.

title: Über das Gravitationsfeld eines Massenpunktes nach der Einsteinschen Theorie
author: Karl Schwarzschild
significance: First exact solution to Einstein's equations — predicted the event horizon. Written in the trenches of WWI
source: Sitzungsberichte der Preussischen Akademie der Wissenschaften (1916)

title: Invariante Variationsprobleme
author: Emmy Noether
significance: Noether's theorem — every symmetry in physics corresponds to a conservation law. The deepest result connecting mathematics and physics
source: Nachrichten der Königlichen Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen (1918)
modernRelevance: Noether's theorem is the reason physicists trust conservation of energy, momentum, and charge -- it underpins the Standard Model, and every gauge symmetry in particle physics exists because of her 1918 insight.

title: A Determination of the Deflection of Light by the Sun's Gravitational Field
author: Arthur Eddington, Frank Dyson, Charles Davidson
significance: Solar eclipse expedition confirmed general relativity — starlight bent by the Sun's gravity as Einstein predicted. Made Einstein world-famous
source: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 220 (1920)

title: Recherches sur la théorie des Quanta
author: Louis de Broglie
significance: Matter has wave properties — electrons have wavelengths. Ph.D. thesis that launched wave-particle duality
source: Annales de Physique 3 (1925); Ph.D. thesis, Sorbonne

title: Über den Zusammenhang des Abschlusses der Elektronengruppen im Atom mit der Komplexstruktur der Spektren
author: Wolfgang Pauli
significance: Pauli exclusion principle — no two fermions can occupy the same quantum state. Explains the periodic table and all of chemistry

title: Über quantentheoretische Umdeutung kinematischer und mechanischer Beziehungen
author: Werner Heisenberg
significance: Matrix mechanics — first complete formulation of quantum mechanics. Replaced classical trajectories with observable quantities only

title: Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem
author: Erwin Schrödinger
significance: The Schrödinger equation — the fundamental equation of quantum mechanics. Equivalent to Heisenberg's matrix formulation but more intuitive
modernRelevance: The Schrodinger equation is solved billions of times daily in computational chemistry software designing new drugs, catalysts, and semiconductor materials.

title: Zur Quantenmechanik der Stoßvorgänge
author: Max Born
significance: Born rule — the wave function gives probabilities, not certainties. Made quantum mechanics fundamentally probabilistic

title: Über den anschaulichen Inhalt der quantentheoretischen Kinematik und Mechanik
author: Werner Heisenberg
significance: Uncertainty principle — you cannot simultaneously know both position and momentum with arbitrary precision. A fundamental limit of nature, not measurement
modernRelevance: The uncertainty principle sets the fundamental noise floor for every quantum sensor, and it is the reason quantum key distribution (QKD) can detect eavesdroppers.

title: The Quantum Theory of the Electron
author: Paul Dirac
significance: The Dirac equation — unified quantum mechanics and special relativity. Predicted antimatter (the positron, found in 1932)
source: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 117 (1928)
modernRelevance: Dirac's prediction of antimatter is confirmed every day at CERN, and positron emission tomography (PET) scans -- which detect antimatter annihilation inside your body -- are a standard medical imaging tool.

title: A Relation between Distance and Radial Velocity among Extra-Galactic Nebulae
author: Edwin Hubble
significance: Hubble's law — galaxies are receding, and farther galaxies recede faster. The universe is expanding. Led to Big Bang cosmology
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 15 (1929)
modernRelevance: Hubble's discovery that the universe is expanding launched Big Bang cosmology and is the reason the James Webb Space Telescope was built to observe the most distant, most redshifted galaxies.

title: Über formal unentscheidbare Sätze der Principia Mathematica und verwandter Systeme I
author: Kurt Gödel
significance: Gödel's incompleteness theorems — any consistent formal system containing arithmetic has true statements it cannot prove. Shattered Hilbert's program
modernRelevance: Godel's proof that consistent formal systems cannot prove all truths is why no software verification tool can guarantee the absence of all bugs -- computability has hard limits.

title: The Maximum Mass of Ideal White Dwarfs
author: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar
significance: Chandrasekhar limit (1.4 solar masses) — above this, white dwarfs collapse. Predicted neutron stars and black holes

title: The Existence of a Neutron
author: James Chadwick
significance: Discovered the neutron — completed the picture of the atomic nucleus (protons + neutrons) and enabled nuclear fission
source: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 136 (1932)

title: Can Quantum-Mechanical Description of Physical Reality Be Considered Complete?
author: Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky, Nathan Rosen
significance: The EPR paradox — argued quantum mechanics is incomplete because of 'spooky action at a distance.' Launched the entanglement debate that's still running

title: On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem
author: Alan Turing
significance: Defined the Turing machine — universal model of computation. Proved the halting problem is undecidable. Founded computer science
source: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society 42 (1936)
modernRelevance: Every computer ever built, from your laptop to cloud data centers, is a physical realization of Turing's 1936 abstract machine -- he defined what computation means before hardware existed.

title: Energy Production in Stars
author: Hans Bethe
significance: Explained how stars shine — the carbon-nitrogen-oxygen (CNO) cycle and proton-proton chain fusion reactions
modernRelevance: Bethe's fusion reaction chains are the same processes that NIF achieved in controlled ignition in 2022, and they inform every NIAC fusion propulsion concept aiming to harness stellar energy for deep-space travel.

title: On Continued Gravitational Contraction
author: J. Robert Oppenheimer, Hartland Snyder
significance: First rigorous prediction that massive stars collapse into black holes — 'the star thus tends to close itself off from any communication with a distant observer'

title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
author: Claude Shannon
significance: Founded information theory — defined the bit, entropy of information, channel capacity. Foundation of digital communication, compression, and cryptography
modernRelevance: Shannon's information theory sets the hard limits on data compression and transmission rates exploited by every streaming service, cellphone modem, and deep-space communication link.

title: Space-Time Approach to Quantum Electrodynamics
author: Richard Feynman
significance: Feynman diagrams and path integrals for QED — revolutionized how physicists calculate and think about particle interactions

title: Quantum Electrodynamics (series)
author: Julian Schwinger
significance: Covariant formulation of QED — renormalization made rigorous. Shared Nobel with Feynman and Tomonaga

title: The Origin of Chemical Elements (αβγ paper)
author: Ralph Alpher, Hans Bethe, George Gamow
significance: Predicted Big Bang nucleosynthesis — the universe's first few minutes produced hydrogen and helium in observed proportions

title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid
author: James Watson, Francis Crick
significance: The double helix structure of DNA — 'It has not escaped our notice that the specific pairing we have postulated immediately suggests a possible copying mechanism'
modernRelevance: The double-helix structure Watson and Crick described is now read by sequencing machines that can decode a full human genome in under 8 hours for roughly $200.

title: Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance
author: Chen-Ning Yang, Robert Mills
significance: Yang-Mills gauge theory — the mathematical framework underlying the Standard Model of particle physics. Every fundamental force (except gravity) is a gauge field
modernRelevance: Yang-Mills gauge theory is the mathematical language of the Standard Model -- every prediction confirmed at the Large Hadron Collider, including the Higgs boson discovery, is a computation within the framework Yang and Mills created.

title: Relative State Formulation of Quantum Mechanics
author: Hugh Everett III
significance: Many-Worlds interpretation — the wave function never collapses, all outcomes are real in branching universes. Initially ignored, now taken seriously

title: Theory of Superconductivity
author: John Bardeen, Leon Cooper, John Schrieffer
significance: BCS theory — electrons form Cooper pairs that flow without resistance. Explained superconductivity after 46 years of mystery

title: Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process
author: Rolf Landauer
significance: Landauer's principle — erasing a bit of information dissipates at least kT ln 2 of energy. Information is physical. Resolved Maxwell's demon
source: IBM Journal of Research and Development 5 (1961)
modernRelevance: Landauer's principle sets the ultimate thermodynamic floor for computation -- as chips approach atomic scales, his limit becomes the hard physical constraint on how energy-efficient computers can ever get.

title: Deterministic Nonperiodic Flow
author: Edward Lorenz
significance: Founded chaos theory — tiny changes in initial conditions lead to wildly different outcomes. The 'butterfly effect'
modernRelevance: Lorenz's discovery of deterministic chaos is why weather forecasts degrade beyond about 10 days, and it drives the ensemble-modeling approach used in modern climate science, orbital mechanics, and turbulence simulations.

title: On the Einstein Podolsky Rosen Paradox
author: John Stewart Bell
significance: Bell's theorem — no local hidden variable theory can reproduce quantum mechanics. Proved Einstein was wrong about EPR. The most profound result in quantum foundations
modernRelevance: Bell's theorem proved quantum entanglement is real and non-local, and it is the theoretical guarantee behind quantum key distribution networks being deployed commercially today.

title: Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons
author: Peter Higgs
significance: The Higgs mechanism — gauge bosons acquire mass via spontaneous symmetry breaking. Predicted the Higgs boson (found 2012)

title: A Schematic Model of Baryons and Mesons
author: Murray Gell-Mann
significance: Proposed quarks — protons and neutrons are made of more fundamental particles. Foundation of the Standard Model

title: A Measurement of Excess Antenna Temperature at 4080 Mc/s
author: Arno Penzias, Robert Wilson
significance: Discovered the cosmic microwave background radiation — the afterglow of the Big Bang. Confirmed Big Bang cosmology
modernRelevance: The CMB radiation Penzias and Wilson stumbled upon is now mapped in exquisite detail by satellites like Planck, and its tiny temperature fluctuations are the seeds from which every galaxy, star, and planet in the universe grew.

title: Gravitational Collapse and Space-Time Singularities
author: Roger Penrose
significance: Penrose singularity theorem — gravitational collapse inevitably leads to singularities. Nobel Prize 2020 (55 years later)

title: A Model of Leptons
author: Steven Weinberg
significance: Unified electromagnetic and weak nuclear forces — the electroweak theory. Cornerstone of the Standard Model

title: Quantum Theory of Gravity (Wheeler-DeWitt equation)
author: Bryce DeWitt
significance: The Wheeler-DeWitt equation — attempt to describe quantum gravity. Implies the 'problem of time' (the universe has no external clock)

title: Renormalization Group and Critical Phenomena
author: Kenneth Wilson
significance: The renormalization group — explained phase transitions and gave a systematic way to handle divergences in quantum field theory

title: Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories / Reliable Perturbative Results for Strong Interactions?
author: David Gross, Frank Wilczek / H. David Politzer
significance: Asymptotic freedom — quarks interact more weakly at shorter distances. Made QCD (quantum chromodynamics) viable. Nobel Prize 2004

title: Black Holes and Entropy
author: Jacob Bekenstein
significance: Black holes have entropy proportional to their horizon area — the first hint that gravity, thermodynamics, and quantum mechanics are deeply connected

title: Black Hole Explosions?
author: Stephen Hawking
significance: Black holes radiate and eventually evaporate — combined quantum mechanics, general relativity, and thermodynamics for the first time. Launched the information paradox
modernRelevance: Hawking radiation unified quantum mechanics, general relativity, and thermodynamics for the first time, and the resulting black hole information paradox remains the central open problem driving quantum gravity research.

title: Experimental Realization of Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen-Bohm Gedankenexperiment
author: Alain Aspect, Philippe Grangier, Gérard Roger
significance: First definitive experimental violation of Bell's inequality — entanglement is real, local hidden variables are ruled out. Nobel Prize 2022

title: Anomaly Cancellations in Supersymmetric D = 10 Gauge Theory and Superstring Theory
author: Michael Green, John Schwarz
significance: First superstring revolution — showed string theory is anomaly-free, making it a viable candidate for quantum gravity

title: Algorithms for Quantum Computation: Discrete Logarithms and Factoring
author: Peter Shor
significance: Shor's algorithm — quantum computers can factor large numbers exponentially faster than classical computers. Threatens all RSA cryptography
source: Proceedings of the 35th Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (1994)
modernRelevance: Shor's algorithm is the reason governments and banks are urgently migrating to post-quantum cryptography -- once a fault-tolerant quantum computer runs it, every RSA-encrypted secret on Earth becomes readable.

title: String Theory Dynamics in Various Dimensions
author: Edward Witten
significance: Proposed M-theory — unified the five string theories into one framework. Second superstring revolution

title: Observation of Bose-Einstein Condensation in a Dilute Atomic Vapor
author: M.H. Anderson, J.R. Ensher, M.R. Matthews, C.E. Wieman, E.A. Cornell
significance: First Bose-Einstein condensate — a new state of matter where atoms merge into a single quantum entity. Predicted by Einstein in 1924

title: The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity
author: Juan Maldacena
significance: AdS/CFT correspondence — a quantum gravity theory in a volume is equivalent to a quantum field theory on its boundary. Most cited paper in high-energy physics
source: Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics 2 (1998); hep-th/9711200

title: Measurements of Omega and Lambda from 42 High-Redshift Supernovae
author: S. Perlmutter et al. (Supernova Cosmology Project)
significance: Discovered the accelerating expansion of the universe — dark energy. Nobel Prize 2011
modernRelevance: The discovery that the expansion of the universe is accelerating revealed that roughly 68% of all energy in the cosmos is dark energy -- a mystery that DESI and Euclid are actively probing right now.

title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe and a Cosmological Constant
author: Adam Riess et al. (High-z Supernova Search Team)
significance: Independent confirmation of accelerating expansion — two teams, same revolutionary conclusion. Nobel Prize 2011

title: A Fast Quantum Mechanical Algorithm for Database Search
author: Lov Grover
significance: Grover's algorithm — quantum speedup for unstructured search (√N vs N). Proved quantum computers offer genuine advantage
source: Proceedings of the 28th ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing (1996)

title: Modular Elliptic Curves and Fermat's Last Theorem
author: Andrew Wiles
significance: Proved Fermat's Last Theorem after 358 years — no three positive integers a, b, c satisfy aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ for n > 2

title: The Entropy Formula for the Ricci Flow and its Geometric Applications
author: Grigori Perelman
significance: Proved the Poincaré conjecture (108 years open) and Thurston's geometrization conjecture. Declined Fields Medal and $1M prize

title: Initial Sequencing and Analysis of the Human Genome
author: International Human Genome Sequencing Consortium
significance: First draft of the complete human genome — 3 billion base pairs, ~20,000 genes. Opened the era of genomic medicine
modernRelevance: The Human Genome Project's $3 billion map of our DNA launched the era of personalized medicine -- today a full genome costs under $200, and CRISPR therapies are already curing genetic diseases it helped identify.

title: Observation of a New Particle in the Search for the Standard Model Higgs Boson
author: ATLAS Collaboration / CMS Collaboration
significance: Discovered the Higgs boson at 125 GeV — confirmed the mechanism that gives particles mass. Nobel Prize 2013
modernRelevance: The Higgs discovery completed the Standard Model's particle zoo, and the LHC's ongoing measurements of Higgs properties are the most promising experimental window into physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: A Programmable Dual-RNA-Guided DNA Endonuclease in Adaptive Bacterial Immunity
author: Martin Jinek, Krzysztof Chylinski, Ines Fonfara, Michael Hauer, Jennifer Doudna, Emmanuelle Charpentier
significance: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing — programmable, precise, cheap. Revolutionized genetics, agriculture, and medicine. Nobel Prize 2020
modernRelevance: CRISPR gene editing, based on this paper's technique, is now in FDA-approved therapies for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia, with hundreds more clinical trials underway.

title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger
author: LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration
significance: First direct detection of gravitational waves — two black holes merging 1.3 billion light-years away. Confirmed Einstein's 100-year-old prediction. Nobel Prize 2017
modernRelevance: LIGO's detection opened gravitational-wave astronomy as an entirely new way to observe the universe, and the LISA space detector launching in the 2030s will extend it to supermassive black hole mergers.

title: First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole
author: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration
significance: First direct image of a black hole — M87*, 6.5 billion solar masses. Earth-sized virtual telescope using interferometry
modernRelevance: The first image of a black hole's shadow matched general relativity's predictions to within measurement error, providing the strongest visual confirmation of Einstein's theory in extreme gravity.

title: First Sagittarius A* Event Horizon Telescope Results
author: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration
significance: First image of Sagittarius A* — the supermassive black hole at the center of our own galaxy, 4 million solar masses

title: Highly Accurate Protein Structure Prediction with AlphaFold
author: John Jumper et al. (DeepMind)
significance: Solved the protein folding problem — predicted 3D structure of nearly all known proteins. Nobel Prize 2024. Arguably the biggest AI contribution to science so far
modernRelevance: AlphaFold has predicted the 3D structure of over 200 million proteins, accelerating drug discovery pipelines that previously took years of crystallography down to minutes of computation.

title: JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES) results
author: Multiple JWST teams
significance: JWST's first deep field images — galaxies from 300 million years after the Big Bang, more numerous and more mature than expected. Challenging galaxy formation models

title: Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment
author: National Ignition Facility team
significance: First controlled fusion ignition — more energy out of the fusion reaction than laser energy in. Major milestone toward fusion energy

title: The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-Wave Background
author: NANOGrav Collaboration
significance: Detected the gravitational wave background — the low-frequency hum of supermassive black hole mergers across the universe

title: DESI 2024 VI: Cosmological Constraints from the Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations
author: DESI Collaboration
significance: Hints that dark energy may vary over time — not a constant. If confirmed, could overturn the simplest cosmological models

title: Quantum Error Correction Below the Surface Code Threshold
author: Google Quantum AI
significance: First demonstration of quantum error correction improving with more qubits — below the threshold needed for scalable quantum computing

title: Attention Is All You Need
author: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar et al.
significance: Introduced the Transformer architecture — the foundation of GPT, BERT, Claude, and the entire modern AI revolution
source: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (2017)
modernRelevance: The Transformer architecture introduced in this paper powers GPT, Claude, Gemini, and essentially every large language model -- it is the engine of the current AI revolution.

title: Generative Adversarial Nets
author: Ian Goodfellow et al.
significance: Introduced GANs — two neural networks competing to generate and discriminate. Foundation of generative AI for images
source: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 27 (2014)

title: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search
author: David Silver et al. (DeepMind)
significance: AlphaGo defeated world champion Lee Sedol at Go — a game previously thought to require human intuition for decades more

title: Deep Learning
author: Yann LeCun, Yoshua Bengio, Geoffrey Hinton
significance: Definitive review of deep learning by its three pioneers (Nobel Prize 2024). Marked the moment the field achieved mainstream scientific recognition
